title: Contents Packout & Storage Storage Billing Rules
content:
## Rules

1. The job must be in in custody or return scheduled status when a storage period is charged.
2. Storage is billed in storage periods of the tier's period length counted from the custody start date, each period billed in full on its first day at the vault rate times the vault count in force that day; climate-controlled tiers bill the climate vault rate and oversized items are billed per item per period.
3. On-site manipulation and in-plant cleaning carry no storage.
4. A storage period whose first day falls on or before the approved storage end date of the linked claim file is billed to the insurance claim, and any other storage period is billed to the customer.
5. A self-pay job's storage is always billed to the customer.
6. A customer-billed period is due the tier's storage invoice due days after its first day, and customer-billed storage left unpaid longer than the tier's referral days is referred to a human collections manager as not covered by policy.
7. When the customer has declared a value, declared-value coverage is billed each period at the tier's valuation percentage of the declared value, rounded to the cent, half up, and always to the customer, because it is the customer's own election.

## Retired clauses

- In rule 2, the clause "each period billed in full on its first day at the vault rate times the vault count in force that day" is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current Contents Packout & Storage basis. Billing storage in storage periods of the tier's period length counted from the custody start date, the climate vault rate on climate-controlled tiers and per-item billing of oversized items remain in force.
- In rule 7, the clause "declared-value coverage is billed each period at the tier's valuation percentage of the declared value, rounded to the cent, half up" is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis. That declared-value coverage is billed when the customer has declared a value, and always to the customer as the customer's own election, remains in force.

## Who a storage period is billed to

The test compares the first day of the period with the approved storage end date on the claim file linked to the job, as the claim file records it.

| Job | First day of the storage period | Billed to |
|---|---|---|
| insurance-funded | on or before the approved storage end date | the insurance claim |
| insurance-funded | after the approved storage end date | the customer |
| self-pay | any | the customer |
| any job carrying declared-value coverage (the coverage line) | any | the customer |

**Boundary case (abstract dates).** A period whose first day is the approved storage end date itself is billed to the insurance claim; a period whose first day is the day after it is billed to the customer.

## Due date and referral of customer-billed storage

A customer-billed period is due the tier's storage invoice due days after its first day. When customer-billed storage stays unpaid longer than the tier's referral days, the account goes to a human collections manager as not covered by policy. The day counts are the tier values on the product's storage rate card.

**Hypothetical illustration.** With a hypothetical due-days figure of 12, a customer-billed period whose first day is the 4th of a month is due on the 16th.

superseded_clauses: each period billed in full on its first day at the vault rate times the vault count in force that day
declared-value coverage is billed each period at the tier's valuation percentage of the declared value, rounded to the cent, half up
